purpose: Validate the task intake to multi-CLI lane initialization graph used by the desktop supervisor.

resource_controls.timeout_policy: Each initialized lane inherits SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS and can be cancelled.
resource_controls.cancellation_policy: The platform can cancel each active session and kill/wait the child process.
resource_controls.cleanup_policy: Session stdin is dropped on finish; stdout/stderr reader handles are joined when finished.
resource_controls.orphan_process_policy: Cancel calls kill and wait the child process; future PTY/process-group cleanup remains a follow-up.
resource_controls.backpressure_policy: stdout/stderr are read on separate threads into bounded buffers to avoid pipe buffer blocking.

merge_strategy: Available lanes initialize independently and flow to a platform merge gate; missing lanes become capability_missing and do not block independent lanes.
plan_evidence: The user requested a pipe-based structure for initializing diverse CLIs from diverse tasks.
The existing desktop backend already uses Rust std::process pipes for single CLI sessions.
The platform-first runtime contract requires external CLIs to remain optional guest adapter lanes.
rollback_plan: Disable the Task Pipe Init UI and keep single CLI session start available.
Keep the requirements/spec additions but mark the task pipe command as deferred if validation fails.
notes: This is a contract validation record. Real CLI execution still depends on user-installed optional CLIs.
